title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
summary: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

title: Lieb-Robinson bounds via the Combes-Thomas estimate
summary: This paper studies quantum spin systems: networks of spins coupled by local interactions. The Lieb-Robinson bound predicts that in these systems, information propagates at an essentially finite speed. We produce a new proof of this result. Our approach relies on a spectral bound on entries of resolvents of band matrices, the Combes-Thomas estimate, rather than on the standard path-counting argument.

title: On the Road Again: How the $N$-Lane TASEP and Local Reservoirs Drive Jamming in Axonal Transport
summary: Intracellular transport by molecular motors along microtubules is essential for cellular function, particularly in neuronal axons where track disruption drives neurodegenerative disease. We develop an \(N\)-track totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) model where motors reversibly detach into local off-track states. Using mean-field, continuum, and fast-switching approximations, we derive an effective nonlinear transport equation for total motor density. This reduced model retains the classical TASEP phase structure but reveals that increasing \(N\) shifts the boundaries between low-density, high-density, and maximal-current regimes. Crucially, under source-driven boundary conditions reflecting constant cargo production, the entrance density undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation when the production rate exceeds the network's transport capacity, \(N/4\). This triggers persistent cargo accumulation that propagates throughout the domain. Our results establish a physical mechanism by which gradual microtubule degradation drives a transition from efficient transport to jammed pathological states.

title: Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schrödinger spectral projections
summary: We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schrödinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and Rényi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.

title: Cross Section Measurements and Searches for New Structures in $e^+e^-$ Annihilations at BESIII
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 46 references, contribution to the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP 2026)
summary: The BESIII collaboration has collected large data samples in the center-of-mass energy range from 1.84 to 4.95 GeV. These data provide a low-background environment and wide energy range for studying the cross sections and the spectroscopy of charmonia. In this article, we review the recent achievements by the BESIII collaboration, including for searching new structures of $XYZ$ particles and the hyperonic production over open-charm threshold.

title: Regular magnetic black holes with anti-de Sitter cores in scalar-tensor gravity with nonlinear electrodynamics: ghost-free construction and axial stability
summary: We construct static, asymptotically flat regular black holes in Einstein-frame scalar--tensor gravity, sourced by a canonical scalar coupled to magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics. Prescribing the density and scalar profiles, we reconstruct the metric, the scalar--photon coupling and the potential. Regularity requires the mass function to vanish at the centre, which fixes the ADM mass, and the central $r^2$ growth of the density to be balanced by the scalar gradient energy. The solutions have an anti-de Sitter core supported by a negative potential and a nearly Reissner--Nordström exterior; the no-ghost condition confines the magnetic charge to a window that closes at a finite core depth. Axial perturbations reduce to a symmetric two-channel master system whose positive-definite potential guarantees mode stability; spectral and time-domain quasinormal frequencies agree. An angular Laplacian instability near the centre can be hidden behind the inner horizon, which excludes horizonless solutions.

title: Non-Geometric Heterotic Vacua from Type II$_0$ Loci
summary: We determine 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ heterotic string backgrounds dual to Type IIB string theory compactified on Calabi--Yau threefolds containing a type II$_0$ locus in their complex structure moduli space. While previous work only established the existence of such a duality frame, we concretely identify the heterotic theories dual to one- and two-parameter models exhibiting such loci, yielding novel instances of Type IIB--heterotic duality. To establish the correspondence, we first match the massless $\mathcal{N}=2$ spectrum, which uniquely fixes the heterotic data. We then recover the light spectrum of BPS D3-branes wrapping cycles on the Type IIB side from the heterotic perspective, and finally match the duality groups governing the global structure of the vector multiplet moduli space. All resulting heterotic theories are genuinely lower-dimensional, as they do not admit a decompactification limit to ten dimensions in their hypermultiplet moduli space. We identify two classes of duals. In the first, the heterotic string is compactified on a geometric K3 with a standard gauge bundle, demonstrating explicitly that type II$_0$ loci admit a consistent description as weakly coupled heterotic strings. In the second, the heterotic string background is given by a string-scale K3 and is hence non-geometric and genuinely four-dimensional. In this case, directly establishing supersymmetry would require control over all perturbative and non-perturbative $α'$ corrections. Here, the duality to Type IIB is most powerful, as it establishes the existence of new consistent, supersymmetric, and anomaly-free heterotic compactifications beyond the reach of conventional geometric methods. Finally, the Type IIB realization of the two-parameter models reveals that four-dimensional heterotic compactifications admit smooth transitions involving the nucleation of NS5-branes.

title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
summary: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.

title: The Lévy wave packet and fractional uncertainty relations
summary: This work revisits the debate on fractional uncertainty relations that arose a decade ago and tries to settle it. After a careful study of the position-momentum uncertainty product of the Lévy wave packet, a novel lower bound is proposed for uncertainty relations in fractional quantum mechanics. This bound is nearly linear in the Lévy index and is satisfied by exact, calculable solutions available in the literature.

title: Study of $Λ$ $CP$ Asymmetry Parameter and Electric Dipole Moment at the Super Tau-Charm Facility
summary: Searching for new mechanisms of $CP$ violation beyond the Standard Model is essential to explain the observed matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe. By analyzing the full angular distribution of the quantum-entangled $Λ\barΛ$ pairs from $J/ψ$ decays, the preliminary sensitivity of $CP$ asymmetry parameter $A_{CP}$ and Electric Dipole Moment of $Λ$ is studied at the future Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF). Based on $3.4 \times 10^{12}$ $J/ψ$ events at STCF, the projected sensitivity for $A_{CP}^Λ$ reaches the $10^{-4}$ level, while the $Λ$ EDM can be probed at $10^{-20}$ $e$ cm. These results highly indicate that STCF will provide an unprecedented opportunity to search for new mechanisms of $CP$ violation with an expected world-leading precision.

title: Learning Parameters of dRGT Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics with Neural Network Scenarios
summary: Using machine learning methods, we present constraining parameter scenarios of AdS black holes in dRGT-like massive gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. We first approach the photon sphere, the black hole shadow, and the energy emission rate with the help of high performance parallel computations. To corroborate such optical results, we develop a numerical framework to constrain the electric charge and the nonlinear electrodynamic parameter, for certain gravity regimes, via the shadow observations reported by the Even Horizon Telescope collaboration. Employing neural networks, we then examine the parameter regions of the black holes based on their consistency with EHT observations of M87$^*$, SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$, and SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{Keck}}$, within the $1-σ$ and $2-σ$ confidence intervals. As a result, we find that the obtained constraints are consistent with the $SgrA^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$ empirical data.

title: De Sitter Observers and an Effective Field Theory of Horizon Edge Modes
summary: We show that choosing a test observer in $dS_D$, specified by the framed embedding of their horizon $S^{D-2}$, spontaneously breaks the de Sitter and internal sphere isometries to diagonal rotations. We identify gravitational edge modes, described by low diffeomorphism jet fluctuations near the horizon sphere, as the associated Goldstone modes. We construct their membrane-like effective theory, organized in a small-gradient expansion. We find a class of nonlinear actions that at the quadratic order reproduce the edge-mode spectrum previously found in the one-loop gravitational $S^D$ path integral.

title: Theory of the intrinsic optical anomalous Hall responses in time-reversal symmetry breaking superconductors
summary: Determining the symmetry of the Cooper pairing in superconductors is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. Time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) is among the most distinctive symmetry-breaking pattern of a superconductor. An important subset of TRSB pairing states, including the topological $p_x+ip_y$ pairing, is expected to exhibit the optical anomalous Hall effect. However, the microscopic ingredients that enable the Hall response and their underlying organizing principle in clean superconductors remain unelucidated. Here, we develop a unified theory for TRSB multiband superconductors possessing inversion symmetry, and establish their intrinsic optical Hall response as fundamentally a quantum-geometric phenomenon. We distinguish unitary and nonunitary TRSB states. Diagrammatically, we identify two classes of processes: single-electron tunneling and Cooper-pair tunneling. Both involve at least one interband tunneling event driven by the interband velocity-which is closely tied to the interband Berry connection. We rigorously prove that interband pairing is a prerequisite for unitary states to generate intrinsic Hall response, whereas it is not absolutely needed for nonunitary states. In nonunitary states with intraband pairing alone, the Hall effect can arise through single-electron tunneling, provided spin-orbit coupling is present. An effective theory obtained by integrating out the hole degrees of freedom reproduces these results and shows how pairing may endow electrons with effective Berry curvature. Finally, through symmetry analysis, we show that intrinsic resonances near the superconducting gap edge are allowed in nonunitary states but forbidden in unitary states. Our work thus establishes quantum geometry as a unifying principle for the intrinsic Hall response in superconductors and provides a guide for distinguishing different candidate TRSB pairings.

title: Geometrization of continuum mechanics and nonequilibrium thermodynamics: Heat conduction
summary: We propose a geometric formulation of non-equilibrium heat conduction. It combines the variational (Hamiltonian) structure of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) equations with the exterior calculus of differential forms. The central object is the thermal impulse one-form on the four-dimensional matter-time manifold. Its time component is the temperature, and for reversible (ballistic) heat transport it is the exact differential of a scalar potential (i.e. it is holonomic). Non-equilibrium effects are described by a second one-form, the small-scale thermal impulse, which is not required to be exact. Its time component is a fluctuating temperature, and its exterior derivative, the four-thermal vorticity, satisfies a Bianchi-type kinematic identity. The variational principle together with this identity yields a non-equilibrium two-temperature model. Its field equations have the same structure as Maxwell's equations in a medium, with the thermal impulse field, the thermal vorticity field and a thermal Poynting vector contributing to the heat flux. Dissipation is introduced through relaxation terms that conserve the total energy and produce entropy. A formal asymptotic analysis shows that, in the relaxation limit, the model reduces to a Guyer-Krumhansl-type heat conduction with independent transverse and longitudinal length scales. The transverse nonlocal term comes from the spatial non-holonomy of the small-scale thermal impulse, while the longitudinal term comes from its non-holonomy in time, i.e. from the relaxation of the fluctuating temperature. We also discuss the gauge-theoretic interpretation of the model. Its kinematics is that of an abelian gauge theory, while the local gauge symmetry is explicitly broken by the existence of two temperatures. Finally, we discuss the consequences of the geometric structure for structure-preserving numerical methods.

title: Unfolding the low-energy reactor neutrino flux from CE$ν$NS data with a finite Dirac sum
summary: We present a novel method to analyze coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) data to extract the reactor antineutrino spectrum below the inverse beta decay threshold of 1.8 MeV, where it remains unmeasured. Adapting halo-independent analysis techniques developed for direct dark matter detection, we show how to obtain a best-fit and a pointwise confidence band for the integrated neutrino flux, without assuming a parametric form or smoothness prior for the spectrum. In our approach, which follows from convex geometry arguments, the differential neutrino rate is written as a linear combination of Dirac delta functions -- a finite Dirac sum (FDS) -- with a maximum number of terms determined by the number of data points. We apply our "FDS method" to mock CE$ν$NS data for a low-threshold Ge detector and compare it with Tikhonov-regularized unfolding.

title: Noisy Pipelines I: An end-to-end pipeline to perform multivariate noise inference for LISA
comment: (13 + 10) = 23 pages, 15 figures, 3 tables, for submission to MNRAS
summary: Instrumental data from the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) must be post-processed prior to any global-fit based analysis. For example, it is critical to filter, downsample, segment and window the data in order to perform inference of both the signal and noise parameters in the frequency domain. Each step alters the noise process, requiring a correction to the noise covariance matrix that describes the underlying data stream. We present $\texttt{lisa-noise}$, a JAX-based noise inference pipeline that returns a spectral estimate of the noise process subject to post-processing effects. We fit splines to the underlying secondary noises and fit the full multivariate $3 \times 3$ covariance matrix of the Michelson channels. We assume unequal and non-constant arm-lengths throughout. The drift of the zeros of the transfer functions, a non-stationary effect, is captured by averaging the transfer functions over a number of epochs within each segment. On 30 days of conditioned simulated data, a likelihood evaluation costs $3\,$ms on a current laptop for a 7 day segment. A gradient-based fit from a tight prior recovers the injected spectra in a fraction of a second. A multi-start search over large priors $\pm 10$ in $\log_{10}$ centred on the simulated truth obtains a noise estimate consistent with the data, verified by Bayesian techniques. The fitted covariance whitens the conditioned data in every band and through every zero of the transfer functions, in a form that global-fit pipelines can use directly.

title: Quasinormal-mode stability bounds in gravitational EFT: resolvability, predictivity, and positivity
summary: It has been proposed that consistency limits how slowly black holes can ring down in extensions of General Relativity: effective-field-theory (EFT) corrections may lengthen the decay time of a quasinormal mode by at most about one oscillation period, $\Re[ω_{\rm GR}]\,δτ\lesssim1$. We argue that, under standard power counting, this condition yields no new, model-independent constraint on gravitational EFTs. First, its motivation does not extend straightforwardly to black holes: the inverse oscillation frequency is not a universal, detector-independent uncertainty in the damping time of a classical waveform. Our main argument, however, rests on eikonal power counting alone. The decay-time shift grows with the angular momentum $\ell$ of the mode, but so does the weight of higher-derivative operators. When curvature and derivatives are controlled by a single scale $Λ$, as in every known ultraviolet completion, the EFT around a black hole of radius $r_s$ remains predictive up to $\ell\sim(r_sΛ)^2$, and the shift becomes of order one only there, where an infinite tower of operators contributes at the same order. A resolvable shift within the predictive regime requires either large numerical coefficients or a two-scale power counting, which has no known ultraviolet completion. In both cases the quartic-curvature operators dominate, and the condition coincides parametrically with the positivity bounds that flat-space graviton amplitudes impose under standard assumptions on the ultraviolet completion. Only in scalar--tensor theories could the two-scale window probe beyond positivity, and then at most one family of dimension-ten operators. The axial sector of Einstein--dilaton--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and Einstein--Maxwell theory illustrate these results.

title: Polymer-Mediated Hotspot Evolution in Shock-Induced Pore Collapse in 1,3,5,7-Tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocane (HMX)-based Explosives
summary: The initiation of detonation in high explosives (HEs) under shock loading is strongly influenced by the collapse of porosity and the subsequent formation of hotspots. As these materials are widely integrated with polymer binders to form polymer-bonded explosives, the collapse of pores at explosive-binder interfaces has received significant interest. Recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that the shock-driven expansion of soft polymers (e.g. polystyrene) into a void produces greater pressure-volume (PV) work during recompression and higher local temperatures compared to pore collapse in neat HEs, ultimately expediting the onset of chemical reactions. Yet how pore collapse, interfacial phenomena, and binder chemistry jointly affect initiation remains insufficiently understood. We provide deeper insights into the role of polymer in hotspot evolution through reactive MD simulations, specifically characterizing its chemical behavior during the shock-induced collapse of voids at sizes approaching experimentally relevant length scales. We consider the HE 1,3,5,7-Tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocane (HMX) in a crystal-gap-crystal stack with polystyrene along the upstream surface. In the hydrodynamic collapse regime, hotspots nucleate at the material interfaces, with void length-dependence in PV work, shock temperature, and the onset of self-sustaining chemistry. Driven by shock-induced deformation and HMX decomposition, the binder undergoes backbone chain scission followed by extensive aromatic-backbone cross-bonding, akin to a graphite to diamond transformation. These reactions act as heat sinks, suppressing deflagration and ultimately inhibiting hotspot growth and coalescence between crystals. The simulations further link the polymer's chemical response to the shock-to-detonation transition in polymer-bonded explosives.

title: On the planar Neumann--Poincaré inverse spectral problem
summary: Does the Neumann--Poincaré spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended Möbius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and Möbius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.

title: Measurement of the neutrino cross section across the TeV scale using IceCube data
comment: Main text is 7 pages, with 2 figures
summary: Neutrinos interact with matter exclusively through the weak force, resulting in extremely small cross sections that are difficult to measure. At TeV energies, neutrino-nucleon interactions probe the structure of the nucleon in regimes where our knowledge of it is less complete, and signatures of physics beyond the Standard Model could manifest. Recent measurements using collider, atmospheric, and astrophysical neutrinos have begun to explore this regime, but no single measurement has provided precise coverage from sub-TeV to tens of TeV, and uncertainties remain at the level of about 20-40%. Here we present a determination of the muon-neutrino-nucleon charged-current cross sections as a function of energy across 150 GeV-40 TeV using eight years of through-going muon neutrino data collected by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. We measure the average neutrino-antineutrino cross section, enabling direct comparison with previous results, and find, for the first time above 1 TeV, mild indications that the neutrino and antineutrino cross sections can be measured separately. The measured cross sections are consistent with Standard Model predictions and are determined with uncertainties below 20% throughout the explored energy range, achieving the most precise characterization of neutrino-nucleon interactions across the TeV scale to date. These results provide a unified measurement of neutrino-nucleon cross sections in this energy regime, connecting accelerator-based and previous higher-energy neutrino observations - thereby advancing high-energy neutrino physics into the precision era.

title: Lamb shift of rotational energy levels in quantum gravity
comment: 26 pages, 2 figures. Authors are in alphabetical order
summary: One of the major challenges of modern foundational physics is the combination of quantum physics and general relativity into a theory of quantum gravity. A severe obstacle are the required extremely high energy scales for direct tests of quantum gravity effects. In recent years, attention has shifted towards near-future experimental predictions of effective or phenomenological models, such as gravitationally induced entanglement or interactions of linearized gravity with non-relativistic measurement devices. These developments motivate us to study the coupling between the quantized metric perturbation and an anisotropic quantum rigid rotor. The intuitive motivation for our study is that a sufficiently heavy rotor consists of a very large number of component systems. Although quantum gravitational effects are completely negligible at the scale of a single atom or molecule, the effects can get amplified by the sheer number of constituents. The resulting effective model describes the gravitational analogue of the angulon quasiparticle excitations discussed in condensed matter physics, suggesting a pathway for future analogue experiments. As a first concrete test of our model, we derive the gravitational Lamb shift for the energy eigenstates of the rotor, which become dressed by a cloud of virtual gravitons. Although the effect is very small, it could provide a concrete test for whether gravity is truly quantum.

title: Twisted Correlators from Harmonic Superspace
summary: We establish a harmonic superspace formulation for $\mathcal N=2$ orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. We account for the orbifold projection by introducing topological defect lines to the planar supergraphs of $\mathcal N=4$ SYM. These twist lines are sourced by twisted sector operators, transparent to vector multiplets but generate orbifold phases when crossed by bifundamental hypermultiplet fields. This formalism establishes a refinement of the orbifold inheritance principle at supergraph level. As a direct application, we compute leading twist-dependent corrections to BPS two- and three-point functions, finding agreement with localisation results in extremal cases and generating new data for non-extremal correlators. We further map these corrections to finite-size effects in the twisted hexagon formalism. This opens a path towards an all-order integrability prescription of orbifold structure constants.

title: Paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$: complete one phonon Raman spectrum
summary: In this study we present a complete first-order Raman scattering spectrum of paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$- a material, where new type of spin texture induced by noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the Néel temperature ($T_N \approx 90$ K) gives rise to unconventional scenario of magnetism. Basic properties of all five phonon modes ($A_g$, $E_g$ and three $T_g$) predicted by the group theory have been successfully approached through polarization, excitation and temperature dependent measurements. In particular, the ever-missing phonon mode of $T_g$ symmetry has been unambiguously resolved in the room temperature Raman spectrum at approximately 107 cm$^{-1}$, just 1.5 cm$^{-1}$ higher in frequency compared to the $E_g$ mode. Density functional theory calculations reproduce the observed Raman-active phonon spectrum and support the assignment of all five first-order Raman modes, including the near-degeneracy of the $E_g$ and one of the $T_g$ vibrations. The calculations further reveal a dense manifold of low-energy antiferromagnetic spin configurations, separated from the ground state by only a few meV per formula unit. Furthermore, strong signals of inelastically scattered light from the paramagnetic (PM) phase of MnTe$_2$ were acquired with long wavelength excitations, i.e. 633 nm and 785 nm, revealing the $2A_g$ overtone at approx. 360 cm$^{-1}$. The enhanced absorption of the light in the near infrared range could be a putative reason behind the anomalous angular dependence of scattered intensity of the highest frequency $T_g$ phonon mode (183 cm$^{-1}$) measured in PM MnTe$_2$ with parallelly aligned polarizers. Finally, upon cooling just below the $T_N$, the measured properties of phonons remained basically unperturbed by the incipient long-range antiferromagnetic ordering.

title: BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy
summary:
We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the
  renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices
  of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald
  summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a
  sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and
  reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for
  all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem
  to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate,
  a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact
  five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.

title: Testing the statistical compatibility of data sets with a common prior
comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Python code provided as ancillary file
summary: The Parameter Goodness-of-fit (PG) test [hep-ph/0304176] offers a simple test statistic to study the compatibility of different data sets within a given theoretical model. In its original formulation it assumes that the data sets are statistically independent. We propose an extension of the PG test for the situation when some parameters of the model are constrained by an auxiliary data set called prior here. As the prior is imposed for all data sets, they are no longer statistically independent. We show that under the Gaussian approximation, the prior-constrained PG test statistic follows a generalised $χ^2$ distribution, which can be used to obtain $p$-values in a straight-forward way. In the approximation of a strong prior constraint, the test converges towards the standard PG test for the unconstrained model parameters.

title: Fields on accelerating and super accelerating black holes: stability, quasinormal modes, greybody factors and strong cosmic censorship
summary: We investigate the propagation of massless scalar, Dirac, and Maxwell fields on accelerating and super accelerating black hole spacetimes described by the C-metric. The latter regime has only recently been identified and remains largely unexplored. We study the linear and mode stability of these backgrounds and derive analytical expressions for the quasinormal mode spectra and greybody factors in various spacetime limits. We classify the quasinormal mode families, paying particular attention to new families arising in the super accelerating regime. We also investigate strong cosmic censorship through Christodoulou's $β$ criterion, finding regions of parameter space where it may be violated, including in the super accelerating regime. These violations are possible for massless scalar and Maxwell fields, whereas Dirac fields preserve the conjecture.

title: de Sitter Gluon Correlators in Momentum Space
summary: We show a new diagrammatic representation of tree-level wavefunction coefficients for gluons in four-dimensional de Sitter space at any multiplicity. Its ``disc diagrams" make the cutting rule manifest, while the remaining contact term is fixed by the absence of folded singularities. We determine this term for configurations with zero, one and two negative-helicity gluons. It simplifies as more gluons share a helicity, and it vanishes for all-plus. We illustrate the expansion at four and five points, attach explicit results up to eight points all-plus, and relate it to Grassmannian residues.

title: Two quantum skyrmions form a magnon Josephson junction
summary: Two quantum skyrmions in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ magnet bind into a molecule, and the molecule acts as a magnon Josephson junction: the relative helicity $θ$ and the number $n$ of magnons transferred between them obey $H=E_Cn^2-W\cosθ$. DMRG on the $J_1$--$J_2$ triangular lattice gives $E_C$ as the curvature of the skyrmion energy at its natural size of seven flipped spins, and the measured helicity coherence fixes $W\simeq0.02J_1$, half the skyrmion--antiskyrmion tunnel splitting and independent of the anisotropy. Two helicity qubits side by side are thus strongly coupled by their own interaction.

title: Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label
summary: We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $ψ_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $ψ_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}ψ_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}ψ_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $ψ_+$ and $ψ_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $π_\hbar$ and $π_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $ψ_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.

title: Radiative corrections to double-$β$ decay and their impact on experimental analyses
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the $\mathcal{O}(α)$ radiative corrections to two-neutrino and neutrinoless double-$β$ decay within a heavy-nucleus effective field theory. We compute all virtual and real-emission corrections for intermediate nuclear states of arbitrary excitation energy, including new closed-form expressions for the required one-loop integrals with heavy-nucleus propagators. For excitation energies large compared with the lepton energies, the corrections factorize into the tree-level rate times a universal double-weak Sirlin function, which differs substantially from the sum of two single-$β$ Sirlin functions used so far in the literature. We discuss the impact of the radiative corrections on the analysis of measured spectra in terms of ratios of nuclear matrix elements, $ξ_{31}$, and show that neglecting radiative corrections can significantly bias the extraction. Real-photon emission, not considered in previous analyses, plays a central role and the impact of radiative corrections depends crucially on the detector setup. We provide the photon spectrum, fully differential in the photon energy and direction, and recommend that experiments simulate the photon explicitly. For $0νββ$ decay, the radiative corrections increase the inclusive rate by about $5\%$, independently of the nuclear matrix elements or the neutrino Majorana mass.

title: Harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--scalar field gravity: exact solutions and regularity
summary: We relate black-hole horizons and wormhole throats to the geometry of the harmonic branches of Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton gravity. In the unified Ernst framework, we first solve the harmonic equations prior to fixing the spatial harmonic, and then jointly reconstruct the metric, Maxwell four-potential, and scalar field. The conserved geodesic energy fixes the meridional Weyl quadrature, whereas the initial geodesic data capture the asymptotic charges. Choosing the Schwarzschild harmonic function, regular nonextremal horizons fix the normalization \(H=1\) along with the associated matter-field regularity requirements. This reproduces the Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordstrom families (including the NUT extension), the Gibbons-Maeda solution, and the dyonic string and Kaluza--Klein solutions, while also preserving their more general branches. If the scalar sector is continued to the phantom sign, one obtains a complementary oblate construction: smooth continuation selects \(H=-1\) and produces the massive and ultrastatic Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes. By comparing with the vacuum ring geometry, we make clear the further importance of the global extension. Altogether, these findings offer a unified black-hole--wormhole geometric reading of the charge relations and regularity constraints for the reconstructed solutions.

title: Orientifold and Integrability: $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super-Yang-Mills on $\mathbb{RP}^4$
summary: We study planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory (SYM) on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^4$ using integrability, holography and supersymmetric localization, and discuss its relation to orientifolds in string theory. We show that the integrability of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM is preserved when combining the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ involution defining $\mathbb{RP}^4$ with the action of the charge conjugation of the SU$(N)$ gauge group. We demonstrate this by calculating one-point functions of non-BPS single-trace operators in various subsectors at weak coupling, which can be mapped to overlaps between energy eigenstates and crosscap states in integrable spin chains. The results exhibit a parity selection rule, a hallmark of integrability, and are given in terms of a ratio of determinants. Building on these results, we conjecture a closed formula for general single-trace operators. We further provide evidence that this construction is holographically dual to a probe orientifold O1-plane in $\text{AdS}_5\times \text{S}^5$ by constructing the corresponding worldsheet crosscap states in the pp-wave limit. Finally, we use supersymmetric localization to compute one-point functions of half-BPS operators exactly at finite $g_{\rm YM}$ and $N$. The computation reduces to two-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ twisted by charge conjugation and leads to a matrix integral of a Wishart-Laguerre type. In the planar limit, the exact result interpolates between the weak-coupling gauge-theory result, the strong-coupling supergravity prediction for the orientifold, and the worldsheet crosscap in the pp-wave limit.

title: Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy of Ce and U Oxides
summary: The soft x-ray Resonant Inverse Photoelectron Spectroscopy (RIPES) of the M5 transition in cerium oxide and the N5 transition in uranium dioxide and supporting instrumentation is discussed. Further experimental evidence and analysis is presented to support the hypothesis that the Ce 5d states are intrinsic to the resonance process in cerium oxide. The strong connection with cerium dioxide is emphasized.

title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
summary: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?
comment: 34 pages, 16 figures, 23 tables. Code and model weights: https://github.com/JayAgarwal25/distilling-jet-taggers
summary: Jet tagging is one of the most important applications of machine learning at the Large Hadron Collider. Recent models build in more physics knowledge or rely on large-scale pretraining, but the experiments place strict limits on their inference cost. Knowledge distillation can transfer their performance to small students that are cheap to run. We ask which properties of a teacher help the student, how small a student can get and how close it can come to the state of the art. On a jet tagging benchmark, we distil six teachers that differ in architecture, symmetry and pretraining, including two foundation models, into five small students. Every teacher improves every student, and the gain depends mainly on the strength of the teacher. We then shrink our two strongest distilled students, Transformer and L-GATr-slim, in width and in depth. With 20 thousand parameters, a distilled L-GATr-slim outperforms every published jet tagger trained from scratch at a fraction of the inference cost of every teacher. Even with two thousand parameters, it matches ParT, a model with a thousand times as many parameters. We also study what the students learn from their teachers. Our benchmark of inference cost shows that students of the same size can differ by almost an order of magnitude in speed. We release the code and the weights of all trained models.

title: Wormholes in Vegh--dRGT massive gravity: a null-energy transparency theorem, horizon obstruction, and exact isotropic solutions
comment: 13 pages, 13 figures. Accepted for publication in Chinese Physics C (2026)
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric wormholes in deRham--Gabadadze--Tolley massive gravity with the spatially degenerate Vegh reference metric. The effective fluid carried by the massive graviton contributes nothing to the combination of density and radial pressure that the flare-out condition constrains, so it is invisible to the null energy condition along radial light rays. This holds for the whole degenerate class of reference metrics, for all four interaction potentials, and for any static spherically symmetric geometry; the same property singles out the Vegh choice as the only consistent one. The matter alone must therefore violate the null energy condition at every throat, exactly as in general relativity. This corrects a claim repeated across the massive-gravity wormhole literature. We then determine where throats may sit. Wormholes with isotropic pressure fall into two families. One lies beyond the cosmological horizon of the theory's own vacuum and has no static exterior; it is empty in general relativity and is switched on by the graviton coupling. The other lies inside that horizon and needs a steeply falling redshift. We give exact perfect-fluid solutions for both. In the second family the graviton term can turn the tension at the throat into ordinary pressure. A thin shell closes the configuration, and its surface stresses and its exotic-matter content follow in closed form. The shells are radially unstable, and light rays near the throat trace an unstable circular orbit.

title: Can componentwise D7-tadpole cancellation yield a chiral Standard Model? A no-go for smooth O7$^{-}$ orientifolds
comment: 8 + 4 pages of main article and an appendix
summary: We study a componentwise prescription for D7-tadpole cancellation that includes, as a special case, the local cancellation used in several moduli-stabilisation constructions. We work in smooth Type IIB Calabi--Yau orientifolds with O7$^{-}$ components of pairwise distinct divisor classes. For each component class $[R_i]$, eight covering-space D7-branes are distributed among smooth irreducible representatives of that class in an orientifold-compatible way. Each component sector may therefore contain several orthogonal, unitary, or symplectic parent factors. We show that these configurations cannot supply the chiral Standard Model through their perturbative D7 spectrum. Without symplectic factors, the entire parent algebra of each component sector embeds into $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ and cannot contain commuting color and weak-isospin subalgebras. Disjointness excludes massless fermions connecting different component sectors, so quark-doublet fermions are absent. Configurations containing symplectic factors require a separate argument: massless hypercharge, together with the same disjointness, forces the net quark-doublet chirality to vanish. Both arguments allow admissible D7 gauge backgrounds and diagonal gauge embeddings, with no restriction on $h^{1,1}_{-}(X)$. We also give a geometric condition under which the tadpole forces purely local cancellation. For a specified finite set of allowed D7 support classes, a separate test identifies component sectors in which the tadpole forces componentwise cancellation. We discuss applications to toric constructions and axion potentials.

title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
summary: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI$_2$ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic exciton transport and highlight the critical role of interface protection in air-sensitive van der Waals materials.

title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
summary:
A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work:
  1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions.
  2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes.
  3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes.
  The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

title: remage: a Geant4-based simulation framework for low-background experiments
summary: Monte Carlo simulations are an essential tool for data modeling and experimental design in low-background physics. These simulations typically demand a considerable effort, with each collaboration developing and maintaining its own complex Geant4 application. In this paper we present the design and validation of remage, which is an open-source framework designed to standardize these simulations and significantly reduce this effort. Its design separates the geometry, built with dedicated Python tools, from the compiled application. It provides a physics list and event generators tuned to radiogenic and cosmogenic backgrounds, output tailored to the most common detector types, and robust validation backed by modern software development practices. The software is distributed ready to use and scales efficiently with the computing resources that demanding simulations require. remage has been primarily developed for the LEGEND experiment, but is applicable to a wide variety of experiments.

title: How general relativity stacks up: Testing gravity by coherently combining gravitational-wave observations
summary: A core mission of gravitational-wave astronomy is to test general relativity (GR) in the high-curvature, high-velocity regime. The field has already seen significant progress in this space, though a remaining challenge is how to combine data from a population of binary mergers. This can both boost the significance of potential GR violations, and develop a phenomenological picture of how deviations manifest in different mergers. We propose a framework to coherently combine gravitational-wave measurements to build a population-level test of physics beyond GR. We assume that deviations from GR are (i) strongest near the merger, (ii) vary smoothly with the total mass of the binary, and (iii) are most prominent in the $\ell=|m|=2$ mode. While these assumptions do not describe every possible deviation of GR, they provide us with a plausible starting point upon which a more general framework can be built. We apply our framework to 28 high signal-to-noise ratio binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, finding no evidence for deviations from GR. Our framework allows one to show how deviations could vary as a function of total mass of the system. We argue that such a reconstruction can be used to convincingly distinguish between systematic waveform errors and genuine GR violations.

title: Circling in on correlation functions in $\mathcal{N}=2$ orbifold theories
summary: We review the harmonic superspace formalism for 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories and apply it to orbifolds of $\mathcal N=4$ Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. These theories have a remarkably similar description to $\mathcal N=4$ SYM, but their planar supergraphs feature topological twist lines which generate phases when intersecting bifundamental hypermultiplet propagators. These cause twisted sector BPS correlators to depend on the coupling $g$. Twisted Coulomb-branch operators of length $L$ receive a leading perturbative contribution to their two-point function at order $\mathcal{O}(g^{2L})$ from a supergraph involving a wrapped hypermultiplet circle. After performing the complete $D$-algebra, we show that the supergraph reduces to the universal conformal period $W_L=\binom{2L}{L}ζ(2L-1)$. We extend this analysis to multiple nested hypermultiplet circles and show that they reproduce a series of higher-order terms in the exact localisation result. A subsequent evaluation of leading contributions to BPS three-point correlators again shows complete agreement with localisation results in extremal case and generates new perturbative data in the non-extremal case. The latter involves one untwisted BPS descendant, which contains physical hypermultiplet fields and can therefore connect directly to the twist-dependent hypermultiplet circle. This reduces the suppression in $g$, resulting in a contribution $4 g^{2(\ell+1)} W_{\ell+1}$ controlled by a bridge length $\ell$ rather than by an external operator length $L\geq\ell$. These examples demonstrate the feasibility of harmonic superspace calculations in orbifold theories and point to various future applications in the context of non-BPS correlators, integrability and marginal deformations.

title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
summary: Silicon nanowires (Si NWs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation nanoelectronic devices due to their tunable electronic properties, and compatibility with aggressive scaling requirements. The integration of strain further enhances their performance by modulating carrier mobility, band structure, and transport behavior without altering material chemistry. Within the NW, the silicon-silicon dioxide (Si-SiO$_{2}$) interface serves as a critical region where strain redistribution and suboxide bonding collectively influence the mechanical and electronic response. Here, we combine reactive force field molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations to investigate how oxidation-induced interfacial structure and crystallographic facet orientation govern strain-dependent bond evolution and facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties in oxidized Si NWs. Simulated dry thermal oxidation generates chemically realistic Si-SiO$_{2}$ interfaces, enabling direct characterization of bond order redistribution and stress gradient development across the interface under tensile strain. Interfacial Si-Si bonds exhibit elongation and reduced bond order associated with partial oxidation states, leading to localized stress concentration and preferential bond rupture. Complementary density functional theory calculations on facet-specific models reveal that orientation-dependent interfacial bonding modulates facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties. Together, these results establish a direct coupling between interfacial suboxide chemistry, mechanical deformation, and electronic structure, providing atomistic insight into strain-modulated behavior at oxidized silicon interfaces in faceted NWs.

title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
summary:
We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$.
  On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

title: Probing New Physics with $b \to u \ell ν_{\ell}$ induced decays
comment: 9 Pages, 1 figure. Submitted to Web of Conference (QCD@Work 2026 Conference Proceeding)
summary: We analyze $B^- \to μ^- \barν_μ$, $\bar{B}^0 \to π^+ μ^-\barν_μ$, and $B^- \to ρ^0 μ^- \barν_μ$ decays using the data on binned branching fractions recently measured by Belle II Collaboration for the semileptonic modes. We extend the low-energy Hamiltonian governing $b \to u \ell \barν_\ell$ transitions to include the full set of dimension-six, Lorentz-invariant operators with left-handed neutrinos, consistent with the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework. The Wilson coefficients are treated as complex, lepton-flavor-dependent effective couplings. Since the three selected channels are sensitive to different non-standard structures, we perform a combined analysis using Monte Carlo methods to constrain the New Physics couplings for three benchmark values of $|V_{ub}|$. We find that, while the Standard Model remains broadly compatible with the data, some of the couplings show a mild preference for non-zero values.

title: Tomimatsu--Sato $δ=2$ Solution in Kaluza--Klein Theory
summary: We construct the Kaluza-Klein electric dressing of the Tomimatsu-Sato $δ=2$ vacuum spacetime by uplifting to five dimensions, boosting along the compact direction and reducing to Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory with coupling $a=\sqrt3$. It carries a nontrivial dilaton, unlike the known Einstein-Maxwell charged and magnetized Tomimatsu-Sato solutions. At leading order it shares the mass-charge-dilaton relations and gyromagnetic ratio $g=2-\tanh^2α$ of the boosted Kerr black hole; the seed first shows up in the quadrupole. Using Mayerson's non-vacuum Geroch-Hansen multipoles, we derive the exact law $M_2(α)=\frac12(1+\cosh^2α)M_2^{(0)}$, so the $δ=2$ quadrupole excess $ΔM_2=-\frac14p^2m^2M$ survives every boost. In the Kodama-Hikida picture the Weyl segment $ρ=0$, $|z|<κ$ is a singular rod with degenerate Killing horizons at its endpoints. There the boost function equals $\coshα$, so the near-horizon geometry is a constant rescaling of the seed's: the horizons stay degenerate and non-rotating, their areas and Komar angular momenta scale by $\coshα$, and the electric potential is $\frac12\tanhα$. The electric flux through any closed surface is $\sinhα\coshα$ times the enclosed seed Komar mass, so the horizons and the ring singularity are uncharged and the rod carries all the charge; the boost-invariant identity $M-Φ_eQ=m$ follows. The ergosurface stays at $f=0$; a new curvature-singular boundary appears at $f=\coth^2α$, where the Kaluza-Klein circle becomes null. As the seed potential $f$ is unbounded above near the ring, it exists for every nonzero boost: unlike for Kerr, no Kaluza-Klein boost of TS$_2$ is a spacelike reduction everywhere. The excised region is compact, has the ring on its boundary and never reaches the horizons. Charging pointwise strengthens the causality violation near the rod.

title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
summary: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $ξ$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $ξ$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.

title: Hereditary Effective Atom Theory for Large-Scale Atomic Structure Prediction
summary: Predicting the atomic structure of large systems requires simultaneous exploration of atomic positions, species, and, generally, the number of atoms. The combinatorial growth of possible arrangements can make this search difficult even for standard genetic algorithms. We introduce Hereditary Effective Atom Theory (HEAT), which integrates Effective Atom Theory into a genetic algorithm to enable efficient global search through a differentiable effective-atom representation. Central to the method is a crossover scheme that directly superimposes two parent structures and relaxes the combined structure. HEAT outperforms conventional genetic-algorithm baselines in recovering a missing 240-atom H sublattice, predicting a 364-atom edge-dislocation core, and reconstructing twisted-bilayer $\mathrm{WSe_2}$ containing 1150 atoms from ptychographic constraints. These results demonstrate how continuous effective-atom relaxation improves the exploration of large combinatorial structure spaces.

title: The Prevalence of Straight Shots in Control Space for Reaching Optimal Quantum Performance
summary: Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape. In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods. In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation. The results show a decrease in the nearest-neighbor distances among straight shots as the sample size increases, suggesting their prevalence in control space. We further conjecture that the starting locations of the straight-shot pathways on a landscape level set may form connected neighborhoods, motivating future investigation into their underlying topological structure. The present paper focuses on the use of STSA for locating massive numbers of straight solutions. However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.

title: Experimental determination of the double $K$-shell vacancy creation probability in the electron-capture decay of $^{55}$Fe with a microcalorimeter
summary: The probability of double \(K\)-shell vacancy production following electron-capture decay is determined for $^{55}$Fe using a high-resolution microcalorimeter. The \(K\)-hypersatellite lines arising from double \(K\)-shell-vacancy filling are directly resolved within the measured spectra of X-ray emissions which are dominated by Mn \(K\)-X-ray diagram lines. The energies of the Mn \textit{K}-hypersatellite lines, \(Kα_2^h\), \(Kα_1^h\), and \(Kβ_{1,3}^h\), are measured as $(6143.5\pm0.5)$ eV, $(6162.1\pm1.5)$ eV and $(6811.9\pm2.6)$ eV, respectively. The relative intensities of \textit{K}-hypersatellite to diagram X-rays are measured to be $(1.30 \pm 0.07) \times 10^{-4}$. From the relative intensities together with established fluorescence yield values, the probability of double-vacancy creation per \(K\)-shell capture ($P_{KK}$) is determined as $(1.22 \pm 0.09) \times 10^{-4}$. Comparisons with previous experimental results and theoretical calculations are discussed.

title: Orientation-dependent sensitivity of the all-sky all-frequency gravitational-wave radiometer search to continuous-wave sources
summary: The all-sky all-frequency (ASAF) gravitational-wave radiometer search cross-correlates the data of two detectors with equal weight on the $+$ and $\times$ tensor polarizations. This is optimal for an unpolarized stochastic background, but not for continuous-wave (CW) sources, whose polarization depends on the inclination angle $ι$ and the polarization angle $ψ$. Unless the source is seen face-on, the search measures less power than a face-on source with the same intrinsic amplitude, and underestimates its strength. The ratio of the two powers, the projection factor $μ^2(ι,ψ)$, is known from earlier radiometer studies. We show how $μ^2$ enters the ASAF statistic, derive its exact dependence on $ψ$, and prove that its average over orientations is exactly $2/5$, independent of sky position, baseline geometry, noise weighting, and frequency. We apply the formalism to four simulated pulsar signals at four sky positions, with polarization from circular to nearly linear, injected into the LIGO detectors during the second observing run (O2). A nearly edge-on injection is measured with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5.20$, below the threshold of $6.19$, while the same signal seen face-on would have an SNR of $31.1 \pm 6.0$. Bayesian upper limits on the strain amplitude $h_0$, marginalized over orientation and calibration uncertainty, are $2.7$ to $2.9$ times the face-on values. For the $505$ sub-threshold candidates of the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run (O4a), the upper limits increase by a factor of $2.5$ to $2.9$, and a source of the same strength would reach threshold only when inclined by less than $34.7^{\circ}$ to $50.3^{\circ}$ from face-on. The measured SNR and the significance of every candidate are unchanged.

title: "Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string
comment: 16 pages, Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference
summary: I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.

title: Influence of embedding depth on the pullout of a plate from a confined granular medium
summary: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. We find that the peak and steady-state drag forces depend differently on their embedding depth for different friction coefficients. Depending on the strength of friction the plate may interact with the domain walls, which enhances the drag force until failure of the aggregate, but not in the steady-state as dilation around intruder directs the force chains emanating from the plate upwards and away from the walls. If the inter-particle friction is weak, it is possible for the overhead pressure to overcome frictional resistance beyond a certain embedding depth. This prevents the formation of dilated failure zones above the intruder and changes the failure mode of the aggregate, leading to a slower decay of the steady-state drag forces with pullout distance.
